extracted.intended_audience: faculty investigators and reviewers preparing or evaluating NIH-style research grants in immunology/biophysics
extracted.subtask_description: A biological/biophysical NIH-style research proposal describing specific aims, significance, innovation, and detailed experimental and modeling approaches to study IgG-FcγR interactions and effector responses across human and murine systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Research Plan required sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists the required Research Plan sections for PHS 398 submissions: 1. Introduction (for Resubmission and Revision applications); 2. Specific Aims; 3. Research Strategy; 4. Progress Report Publication List; Other Research Plan Section items: 5. Vertebrate Animals; 6. Select Agent Research; 7. Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan; 8. Consortium/Contractual Arrangements; 9. Letters of Support; 10. Resource Sharing Plan(s); 11. Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources; 12. Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each numbered section should be included as required (may be uploaded as separate PDFs). Use these headings and include all applicable items (e.g., vertebrate animals, consortium language, resource sharing, authentication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims should state hypothesis and measurable aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims present a central hypothesis and discrete aims (here: Aim 1 Validate a multivalent binding model; Aim 2 Map human and murine IgG isotypes according to conserved effector response; Aim 3 Link IgG effects and in vivo efficacy to identify and verify synergistic IgG-elicited cell killing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be hypothesis-driven, concise, and include clear sub-tasks (measurements, modeling, validation). Use bullet points to list testable experiments or analyses under each aim as shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 1 — experimental validation of multivalent binding model
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 1: Validate a multivalent binding model’s ability to predict FcγR binding to mixed IgG composition immune complexes. Hypothesis: An equilibrium multivalent binding model accurately represents FcγR interaction with ICs of mixed IgG composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (a) Measure mixed composition synthetic IC binding to cells of defined FcγR expression; (b) Generalize the multivalent binding model to account for mixed composition; (c) Fit and verify model predictions of effector response in vitro (PBMC-derived effector populations). Specify cell lines, valencies, mixture ratios, replicates, and planned analyses (ranking correlations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 2 — interspecies mapping by tensor decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 2: Map human and murine IgG isotypes to one another according to conserved effector response. Hypothesis: Murine/human effector response regulation is conserved at the level of cell population responses even when single IgG isotypes are not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a data compendium of predicted effector responses (varying IC concentration, valency, composition, cell populations). Use canonical polyadic (CP/PARAFAC) decomposition to reduce dimensionality and build a map for regulation. Determine number of factors needed to capture >95% variance and correlate factor components between species (Pearson correlation with family-wise error control).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 3 — in vivo linkage and synergy validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 3: Link IgG effects and in vivo efficacy to identify and verify synergistic IgG-elicited cell killing. Hypothesis: A binding model can identify synergistic effector interactions in vivo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regress single IgG treatments and in vivo cell clearance to identify synergistic combinations; verify predicted synergistic cases in in vivo models (platelet and B cell depletion); identify relevant cell populations and mechanisms. Include selection of mixtures based on model predictions and validate in murine models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model construction: two-step multivalent binding process
rubrics_metrics.description: Model FcγR engagement as a two-step process: an initial monovalent interaction followed by multivalent interactions governed by a partition coefficient Kx (the two-step model illustrated in fig. 2B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the model structure follows this two-step formulation and that subsequent binding events are parameterized by Kx. Use branching-process calculations to handle combinatorial microstates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermodynamic consistency: Kx proportional to affinity
rubrics_metrics.description: Kx must be proportional to the affinity of the receptor to satisfy thermodynamic laws (detailed balance): Kx ∝ affinity (Ka).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce proportionality between Kx and measured affinities in the model; deviations from the expected proportional relationship should be interpreted as synergy/antagonism and investigated, but the baseline model should satisfy detailed balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinatorial calculation via branching processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use branching processes to efficiently calculate macroscopic binding when the number of microstates explodes for mixed-composition immune complexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement branching-process probability calculations rather than enumerating all microstates to keep computation tractable; highlight that no additional parametric uncertainty is introduced relative to the published single-IgG model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse of published parameterization where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of model structure, predictions can often be made using previously published parameterization without fitting new parameters; only one Kx* may need fitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start predictions from published parameters and fit only minimally required parameters (e.g., Kx*). Perform fitting where necessary to refine predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify receptor abundance for cell lines and primary cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify receptor abundance in each cell line or primary effector population by staining (FITC-coupled antibodies against FcγRs) and absolute quantitation using beads with defined antibody binding sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain absolute receptor numbers per cell using bead standards; re-sort cell lines with multi-modal distributions or variance >50% of expression level to ensure precise expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHO cell panel and receptor-specific measurement standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a panel of CHO cell lines each expressing a single human FcγR (FcγRIA, FcγRIIA-131H, FcγRIIA-131R, FcγRIIIA-158V, FcγRIIIA-158F, FcγRIIB) and quantify binding with PE-conjugated goat anti-human IgG F(ab’)2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure standardized reagent clones and quantitation approaches; run appropriate replicates and controls; address known unreliable affinity cases (e.g., hFcγRIIIA-158F/hIgG4) by checking source affinity data consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immune complex (IC) assembly and replication standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble ICs using TNP-conjugated BSA at valencies of 4 and 26; create mixed-isotype complexes (all pairs of 5:1 and 1:1 hIgG isotype mixtures, in duplicate). With four IgGs, six hFcγRs, and replicates this corresponds to 528 independent binding measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify valency, concentration, mixture ratios, and replicate structure explicitly; plan experiments to cover combinatorial space while reporting total number of independent measurements to show statistical power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glycovariant mixture experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the effect of IgG glycovariants (especially fucosylated/afucosylated variants) by using antibody production in fucosyltransferase-deficient cell lines (LEC13 CHO cells) and testing pairs of 10:1, 3:1, and 1:1 hIgG1 glycovariant mixtures on hFcγRIIIA-expressing cell lines in triplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus initially on hFcγRIIIA, then extend to other isotypes depending on outcomes; report ratios and replicates; use these data to assess manufacturing-relevant variation in glycoform abundance.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro effector response validation in PBMC-derived populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate model predictions by stimulating separated/differentiated PBMC effector populations (monocytes, macrophages, NK cells) with the same synthetic IC complexes and measuring effector responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure a panel of >5 cytokines (including IL-6 and IFNγ) by bead-based ELISA to ensure results are not cytokine-specific. Use both cytokine secretion and phagocytosis assays to verify functional predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and number of IC mixtures for validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Select ten IC complex mixtures with large predicted variation for in vitro testing (Aim 1.3); for murine validation, select five mIgG1/2c mixtures with large variation in predicted response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use model predictions to choose mixtures that maximize the ability to detect agreement/disagreement; test each mixture across relevant cell types and in replicates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative ranking analysis using Spearman correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the model’s predictive capacity by comparing predicted and actual ranking (Spearman correlation) of response strength to the selected mixed ICs within a cell population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report Spearman correlation values for each cell population to demonstrate rank-order predictive performance; ensure appropriate sample sizes for reliable ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phagocytosis and internalization assay criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify phagocytosis of fluorescently labeled ICs by using intracellular vs extracellular FACS staining for FITC to distinguish surface-bound versus internalized antigen; use cyto-spins and immunofluorescence microscopy as independent verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine flow cytometry and microscopy to corroborate phagocytosis data; include appropriate controls for extracellular quenching and imaging validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption for effector response calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume effector response is proportional to the amount of activating receptor multimerization minus the amount of inhibitory receptor multimerization found in bound complexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State this parsimonious construction explicitly and consider exploring alternative constructions if predictions diverge from observations; document assumptions and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigating discrepancies and alternative mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If binding measurements do not match model predictions, investigate whether discrepancies are limited to subsets/outliers or are global; check underlying affinity measurements and consider additional regulatory mechanisms (e.g., inside-out signaling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single-IgG measurements as controls to localize issues as modeling or experimental problems; employ blocking antibodies targeting each FcγR to isolate individual receptor contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of blocking antibodies to dissect receptor contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a panel of blocking antibodies targeting each FcγR to isolate the influence of each FcγR expressed within a cell population when investigating mechanistic causes of divergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use blocking antibodies as a mechanistic follow-up to determine receptor-specific contributions; include proper isotype and unstimulated controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulate broad combinatorial parameter space for mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulate every possible combination of cell population (eosinophils, NK cells, DCs, neutrophils, classical and non-classical monocytes), valency (1–26), concentration (log-scaled, 1 fM–1 µM), and IgG composition (combinations such as 1:1, 1:2, 1:5, 1:10) to create ~100,000 predicted values per species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comprehensive simulated grids to build the data tensor used for factorization; document simulation ranges and resolutions to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor factorization (CP/PARAFAC) and factor selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition to reduce the four-dimensional predicted-response tensor into component factors; select a sufficient number of factors to capture >95% of the variance in predicted response for each cell population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report number of factors chosen, variance captured, and interpretability of components; show parallel plots and component-variable contributions to enable design insights (which mixtures drive movement along components).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-species correlation testing with family-wise error control
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlate each component of the cell population factorization between species to identify conserved regulation. Test significance with Pearson correlation and control family-wise error rate via cell population randomization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement family-wise error control (e.g., permutation/randomization over cell populations) when testing multiple component correlations to avoid false positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data and comparators from prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage previously published single-IgG binding and in vivo prediction results as comparators to verify new multi-IgG implementation and to detect outliers or inconsistencies (e.g., known unreliable affinity cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare new model outputs against previously validated single-IgG cases to ensure consistency; use prior data to guide troubleshooting and parameter checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental replication and variance control
rubrics_metrics.description: Use replicates (duplicates/triplicates as specified), sort cell lines with high variance, and quantify error bars (standard error of triplicate measurements) to demonstrate measurement precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define replicate strategy per assay (e.g., triplicates for binding and glycovariant assays) and include criteria for re-sorting or repeating assays when variance thresholds (e.g., >50%) are exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of cytokine panel to avoid cytokine-specific bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure a panel of >5 cytokines (including IL-6 and IFNγ) in parallel by bead-based ELISA to ensure results are not specific to a single cytokine and to assess consistency across IC-responsive cytokines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a broad cytokine panel relevant to effector responses and report that rankings and trends are consistent across multiple cytokines to strengthen conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation criteria: interdisciplinary and method-development focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation should emphasize convergence of immunology, data analysis, biophysics, simulation, and experiment to build a predictive, mechanism-based, quantitative picture of IgG-mediated cell killing and methods with applicability to other receptor-ligand families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight novel modeling (branching processes, tensor factorization), applicability to other receptor systems, and potential to inform therapeutic engineering and manufacturing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance criteria: therapeutic potential and practical implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance should explain how understanding mixed Fc interactions will improve antibody engineering, inform endogenous immune response interpretation, guide manufacturing (glycoform mixtures), and aid biosimilar evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear translational impacts: improve matching of effector cell-mediated killing during manufacturing, evaluate biosimilars for low-abundance glycoforms, and propose how IgG-mediated logic could enable combinatorial targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification elements: graduate student fee remission and indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Request funds for Graduate Student Researcher fee remission for one graduate student for three academic quarters for all 4 years, anticipate tuition increases at 3% annual inflation; define MTDC as total direct costs minus graduate student non-resident tuition and fee remissions for two graduate students; indirect cost rate pertains to a percentage of the modified total direct costs (MTDC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the number of GSR quarters requested, inflation assumptions, and how MTDC and indirect costs are calculated; document these definitions in the budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development/mentoring plan expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral trainee participation in career development programs similar to FASEB's individual development plans, including mentoring by two faculty members, annual meetings to discuss career options, and a variety of soft-skill courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe mentoring structure (at least two faculty mentors), frequency of career development meetings, and participation in formal IDP-like programs and training activities.
